skill.name: altorank
skill.description: Use AltoRank's tools to audit whether AI assistants can read a site, propose missing JSON-LD, read Search Console, research keywords, move the content plan, and write SEO drafts into a person's review queue. Use when the user asks about SEO, AI-search (GEO) readiness, Search Console numbers, keywords, or drafting articles for their site. Never publishes or approves.
skill.summary: Guide AltoRank site readiness checks, Search Console analysis, keyword planning, and SEO drafts with human review.
skill.author: altorank

The document requires human confirmation for writes and spending; remote MCP implementation and enforcement are outside this review.

content.user_title: Audit SEO Readiness and Prepare AltoRank Drafts
content.value_statement: SEO decisions become difficult when site readiness, search metrics, and content plans are disconnected. This skill guides AltoRank tools to assess readiness, interpret stored metrics, and prepare drafts for human review.
actual_capabilities: Guide public-domain readiness checks, JSON-LD proposals, and machine-readable content generation through AltoRank tools.
Read connected account workspaces, quota, and CMS connection status.
Interpret stored Search Console performance, cannibalization, coverage, and URL inspection results.
Research keyword candidates and generate individual SEO drafts after consent, returning editor links for human review.
Preview and apply confirmed replacements in eligible drafts, including bulk replacements.
Manage unwritten keyword plans and workspace pauses, and retry failed publication of previously approved articles under documented permission checks.
limitations: Requires the AltoRank MCP server; workspace operations depend on account access, and writes require OAuth write permission.
Cannot approve, delete, or newly publish drafts; publication retries apply only to previously approved articles whose publication failed.
Search Console tools read stored data and do not request fresh measurements from Google.
Research and drafting consume credits or quota; this package contains guidance, not the MCP server implementation.

use_cases.title: Assess Public Site Readiness
use_cases.description: Check a public domain for AI-search readiness and propose structured data before investing in new content.

use_cases.title: Interpret Search Performance
use_cases.description: Review stored Search Console results while distinguishing missing data, measured zeros, and incomplete comparisons.

use_cases.title: Prepare Drafts for Review
use_cases.description: Select an eligible keyword, approve quota use, and generate a draft that remains in the human review queue.

prompt_templates.title: Check Site Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check AI-search readiness for [public domain]. Summarize measured issues and propose JSON-LD improvements. Do not change the site.

prompt_templates.title: Review Search Console Data
prompt_templates.prompt: For [workspace] and [date range], summarize stored Search Console performance and coverage. Distinguish unavailable data from measured zeros and flag incomplete comparisons.

prompt_templates.title: Generate One Review Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: For [workspace], list eligible keywords. Ask me to confirm one keyword and quota use before generating one draft. Return its review link without publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a draft with spending consent.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Coordinated Content Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: In [workspace], preview replacing [old phrase] with [new phrase] across eligible drafts. Propose unwritten keyword-plan changes. Wait for confirmation before applying any changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate draft edits and content planning.

output_examples.input: Explain the report when Search Console is connected but nothing has synced for the selected window.
output_examples.output: Search Console is connected, but no data has synced for this window. Traffic is unknown, not zero. No performance conclusion is available.

output_examples.input: Explain what happens after a confirmed draft request finishes successfully.
output: The draft is ready for human review.
The response includes the article editor link returned by AltoRank.
No publication or approval was performed.

output_examples.input: A draft-generation request timed out. What is the next step?
output_examples.output: A timeout does not prove failure. Retry with the same idempotency key to avoid requesting a duplicate draft.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, permitted mutations, and spending limits before requesting writes or paid research.
Preview replacements and obtain confirmation before applying changes; reuse the same idempotency key after draft timeouts.
Report only tool-provided metrics, preserve unknown states, and return editor links for human review.
anti_patterns: Treating unavailable or unsynced Search Console data as measured zero traffic.
Creating duplicate drafts with fresh retry keys or enabling overage without explicit consent.
Bypassing denied mutations or attempting to approve, delete, or newly publish drafts.

faq.question: Does this skill publish articles automatically?
faq.answer: It cannot newly publish or approve drafts. A separate retry tool can repeat failed publication for an article a person already approved.

faq.question: Can I check a site outside my workspace?
faq.answer: Yes. Readiness checks, schema proposals, machine-readable generation, and readiness reports support any public domain.

faq.question: What access does the skill require?
faq.answer: It requires AltoRank MCP tools. Workspace operations use your account connection; write operations require opt-in OAuth write access.

faq.question: Does it fetch live Search Console data?
faq.answer: No. The documented tools read stored data. Missing syncs and unavailable connections must not be reported as zero traffic.

faq.question: Can research or draft creation incur charges?
faq.answer: Keyword suggestions consume credits, and drafts consume quota. The skill requires consent before spending and explicit approval for overage.

faq.question: Can it edit already published articles?
faq.answer: No. The documented replacement tools refuse approved, scheduled, and live articles. Eligible draft edits require a preview and confirmation.
